project: Finding high-Tc superconductors with AI-designed models
summary: Predict Tc for conventional and unconventional superconductors from crystal structure, screen open databases for high-Tc candidates, and probe what the models learn about pairing mechanisms.

stages.name: Direction and plan
stages.detail: Machine learning for superconductors with open materials foundation models

stages.name: Compute environment
stages.detail: Training runs on GitHub Actions; setting up this repository and the desktop app

stages.name: Electron–phonon data
stages.detail: 7,582 Alexandria entries kept for training (of 8,253); 1,032 JARVIS entries held out as the locked test set; Tc recomputed with mu* = 0.1

stages.name: Measured-Tc data, including unconventional
stages.detail: 2,123 measured Tc for cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other oxides (1,395 superconducting) from 3DSC, which matches SuperCon to Materials Project structures; graded anchors for later discoveries

stages.name: Baseline models
stages.detail: Electron-phonon baseline (gradient boosting, composition + structure) and measured-Tc baseline (composition only, 15.0 K on unconventional families) done

stages.name: AI-designed models
stages.detail: Storm 1.0 for conventional superconductors is in use; Storm round 3 (calibration to measured Tc) and Hurricane for unconventional superconductors are training; Radar, which picks the model, comes next

stages.name: Locked evaluation
stages.detail: 626 dynamically stable JARVIS materials for electron–phonon; leave-one-family-out tests for unconventional families

stages.name: High-Tc screening
stages.detail: Score candidate structures from open databases; shortlist high predicted Tc with low uncertainty for DFT or experimental follow-up

stages.name: Public v0.1

stages.name: Mechanism analysis
stages.detail: Compare electron–phonon Tc with measured Tc to flag materials phonons can't explain, and test known structure–Tc correlations within families

ai_model.name: Storm
ai_model.about: Storm is the project's AI-designed Tc model for conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors; it is trained on DFT electron-phonon data, so it does not cover cuprates, nickelates, iron-based or other unconventional superconductors, which are planned for a separate model, Hurricane. An AI agent (Claude) proposes each design; every candidate is trained and scored with the same composition-grouped cross-validation, and a new version is released only if it beats the current best on average and in at least 4 of the 5 folds, and does not do clearly worse on replicated measured Tc.

changes: Adds 11 physics features proposed by the AI: valence electrons per atom and the distance to Matthias's two Tc peaks, d- and p-block shares, light-atom share, an M^-1/2 phonon scale, a stiffness-over-mass proxy, mass ratio, electronegativity spread and packing fraction
Deeper trees: up to 63 leaves (was 31), at least 10 materials per leaf (was 20)

items.why: valence electrons per atom; Matthias found Tc peaks near 4.7 and 6.5 in transition-metal compounds

items.name: matthias_d47
items.why: distance of the valence-electron count from the first Matthias peak (4.7)

items.name: matthias_d65
items.why: distance from the second Matthias peak (6.5)

items.name: d_fraction
items.why: share of d-block atoms, a proxy for a high density of states at the Fermi level

items.name: p_fraction
items.why: share of p-block atoms (covalent bonding, as in MgB2 and the A15 compounds)

items.name: light_fraction
items.why: share of light atoms (Z <= 9), which vibrate at high frequency

items.name: inv_sqrt_mass
items.why: composition average of M^-1/2; phonon frequencies scale like M^-1/2 (isotope effect)

items.name: omega_proxy
items.why: M^-1/2 divided by the mean nearest-neighbour distance, a crude stiffness-over-mass frequency scale

items.name: mass_ratio
items.why: heaviest over lightest atomic mass; light atoms in a heavy matrix give separate optical modes

items.name: x_diff
items.why: electronegativity difference, a proxy for ionicity and charge transfer

items.name: packing_fraction
items.why: atomic-sphere volume over volume per atom, a proxy for how compressed the lattice is

method.name: Gradient-boosting correction
method.about: small trees learn log(1 + Tc_measured) - log(1 + Tc_Storm) from Storm's outputs and composition

data.source: 3DSC_MP conventional classes (Other, Chevrel, Carbon), not synthetically doped, matched to Alexandria by composition; polymorphs pooled (median)
data.inputs: Storm 1.0 out-of-fold predictions of Tc, λ and ω_log (never the DFT labels)

leaderboard.name: Physics map: rescaled λ and an effective μ*

calibration.rule: release the lowest-error map that beats uncalibrated Storm 1.0 on average and in at least 4 of 5 folds, with at least 25 matched materials
calibration.caveat: SuperCon Tc is averaged over reports, a composition can stand for several polymorphs, and non-superconducting entries are only as good as the lowest temperature measured

model_family.text: Learns from about 7,600 materials whose electron–phonon coupling λ and phonon scale ω_log have been computed (the Alexandria set), then a calibration learned from 298 measured superconductors maps its prediction to measured Tc: off by 1.6 K on average against 2.2 K uncalibrated and 2.5 K for the DFT labels themselves. Our AI agent designed it.

Learns from 2,123 measured Tc values (cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other oxides; SuperCon with Materials Project structures via 3DSC), including 728 materials that did not superconduct. For compounds whose parent it never saw in training it is off by 12.7 K on average, against 15.0 K for a composition-only baseline. Predicting a whole family it never saw is much harder: trained without any cuprate, it misses cuprates by 35 K. Our AI agent designed it.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.about: Hurricane is the project's AI-designed Tc model for unconventional superconductors: cuprates, iron- and nickel-based pnictides and chalcogenides, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides. No first-principles theory gives their Tc, so it learns from measured Tc (SuperCon, with Materials Project structures, via the 3DSC dataset), including materials that did not superconduct. An AI agent (Claude) proposes each design; candidates are scored with cross-validation grouped by parent compound, and a version is released only if it beats the reference on average and in at least 4 of 5 folds.

data.source: 3DSC_MP (SuperCon measured Tc matched to Materials Project structures)
data.cite: T. Sommer et al., 3DSC - a dataset of superconductors including crystal structures, Sci. Data 10, 816 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02721-y; data CC BY 4.0, github.com/aimat-lab/3DSC

inputs.label: Composition statistics
inputs.detail: mean, spread, min and max of 8 element properties, plus the number of elements

items.name: crystal system and lattice centring
items.why: seven crystal systems and four centring types, one-hot

items.name: pg_order
items.why: order of the point group, a single number for how symmetric the crystal is

items.name: vpa
items.why: volume per atom

items.name: density
items.why: density from the composition and the volume per atom

items.name: aniso
items.why: longest over geometric mean of the two shorter reduced-cell edges, a measure of layering

items.name: c_over_a
items.why: c/a of the conventional cell for tetragonal and hexagonal crystals (1 for cubic)

items.name: f_spacing
items.why: volume per f-electron atom to the power 1/3, a proxy for the f-f distance that decides whether f electrons stay local (the Hill limit)

inputs.label: Physics features proposed by the AI

items.name: tm_d
items.why: d electrons per transition-metal atom from charge balance (Cu2+ is d9, Fe2+ d6, Ni+ d9); each family's parent compound sits at a characteristic filling and doping moves it away

items.name: p_cu
items.why: holes per Cu from charge balance (negative for electron doping); cuprate Tc rises and falls with it

items.name: dome
items.why: the empirical cuprate dome 1 - 82.6 (p - 0.16)^2 (Presland and Tallon), largest at p = 0.16

items.name: cu_layers
items.why: Cu atoms per formula unit, a proxy for the number of CuO2 planes; Tc rises from one to three planes

items.name: heavy_block
items.why: share of Hg, Tl, Bi and Pb, the heavy-metal charge reservoirs of the highest-Tc cuprates

items.name: fe_based
items.why: iron or nickel together with a pnictogen or chalcogen, the FeAs- or FeSe-type layer

items.name: f_share
items.why: share of atoms with a partly filled f shell (Ce, Yb, U, Pu and others), the local moments of heavy-fermion metals

items.name: f_count
items.why: nominal f-electron count of those atoms

items.name: mag3d
items.why: share of magnetic 3d atoms (V to Cu), a proxy for spin fluctuations

items.name: nonint
items.why: share of non-integer stoichiometry, which marks doped samples

items.name: n_atoms_fu
items.why: atoms per formula unit as written, a measure of chemical complexity

items.name: oxide
items.why: share of oxygen

items.name: chalcogenide
items.why: share of S, Se and Te

items.name: pnictide
items.why: share of P, As and Sb

items.name: halide
items.why: share of F, Cl, Br and I

inputs.label: Element fractions
inputs.detail: the share of each element seen in at least ten training compounds
